panel.summary: Nothing in the repo registers the Yorkie event webhook for local dev or the integration lane, so the feature is inert outside the production cluster
panel.evidence: The design doc (documents-last-modified.md, Ops section) and the task plan both defer webhook registration to a manual `yorkie project update` with cluster access. docker-compose.yaml only starts `yorkieteam/yorkie:latest` with no project/webhook configuration, and no dev-setup docs were updated, so locally and in the Postgres/Yorkie integration lane `updatedAt` never advances on content edits — the acceptance behaviour ('list reflects real edit recency') cannot be exercised anywhere in-repo.

coderabbit.summary: Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.detail: **Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.** When `data` is empty, the current code calls `prisma.document.update({ data: {}, where })`. Prisma 6.6.0 may reject an empty `data` object at the client-validation level or generate invalid SQL (an `UPDATE` with no `SET` columns). The test mocks `prisma.document.update` so it wouldn't catch a real runtime failure. Returning the existing row via `findUniqueOrThrow` avoids the risk entirely and skips a needless write.
coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts::consider using `finduniqueorthrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
